items.prompt: Mañana ___ doy el regalo a mi hermano.
items.explanation: The person who receives something is the indirect object: le doy (to him).
optionNotes: Lo is the direct pronoun (him, it), not “to him”.
La is the direct pronoun (her, it).
Les is plural; mi hermano is one person.

items.prompt: Mis primos viven en Lima. ___ escribo cada semana.
items.explanation: Escribir a alguien takes an indirect object; for several people: les.
optionNotes: Le is for one person; mis primos are several.
Los is the direct pronoun (them), not “to them”.
Lo is the direct pronoun and singular.

items.prompt: You ask a friend to pass you the salt. You say:
items.explanation: To me = me, before the verb: ¿Me pasas la sal?
optionNotes: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb.
Le would mean “to him” or “to her”.

options: Le voy a escribirle a Ana.
Voy le a escribir a Ana.
Voy a escribir le a Ana.
items.explanation: With an infinitive, the pronoun is attached to it (escribirle) or goes before ir (Le voy a escribir), never twice.
optionNotes: The pronoun cannot go between voy and a.
An attached pronoun is written together with the infinitive: escribirle.
